span.p: class-level on 9 admin controllers, plus one method in AdminMaqamAPI

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: every other guarded handler — including all of AdminUserAPI, where a method-level hasAuthority('user:…') replaces the class-level ADMIN gate rather than adding to it, which is what lets an admin delegate user:read without handing over ROLE_ADMIN

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: yes

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: no — AccessDeniedException from the method-security interceptor, thrown inside the dispatcher and caught by the advice

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: denial raised at the filter layer instead, before any controller is resolved

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Authenticated request carrying a JWT

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: JWTAuthenticationFilter: token verified and not blacklisted, then UserDetailsService.loadUserByUsername reloads the account — SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS, so this happens on every request and nothing is cached

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: UserService.loadUserByUsername runs userRepository.findByUsername: users_tbl plus the EAGER user_permissions element collection, and returns the User entity itself as the UserDetails

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: User.getAuthorities: role.getAuthorities plus every non-null, non-blank string in extraPermissions

div.style: color: rgb(74, 58, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Which Role sits on the user row

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: ADMIN is declared EnumSet.allOf(Permission.class), so the role alone yields every resource:action string

div.style: color: rgb(43, 54, 68) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: AdminUserService.grantPermissions and revokePermissions refuse an ADMIN target: IllegalAdminOperationException ADMIN_PERMISSIONS_LOCKED, mapped to 409 CONFLICT

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: EMPLOYEE and TEACHER are declared Set.of() — the role contributes nothing but its tag, so the whole set comes from extraPermissions rows

div.style: color: rgb(43, 54, 68) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Provisioning time, not request time: User.applyRoleDefaults seeds extraPermissions, and only while that set is still empty. EMPLOYEE_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS is 29 strings — read, create and update on audio, video, image, text, category, person, project, maqam and physical_media, plus physical_media:import and maqam:teacher_manage, never remove or delete. TEACHER_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS is maqam:read and maqam:vote. Admins grant and revoke rows afterwards

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: GUEST is Set.of() and defaultExtraPermissions returns Set.of() for it — never seeded, so it carries the role tag and nothing else

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Role.getAuthorities always appends ROLE_ plus the enum name, so ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_EMPLOYEE, ROLE_TEACHER or ROLE_GUEST rides alongside the resource:action strings

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: SecurityContextHolder holds one flat List of SimpleGrantedAuthority — the ROLE_ tag and the resource:action strings sit side by side with no hierarchy between them

div.style: color: rgb(74, 58, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Which expression guards the method — Spring takes the method annotation if there is one and only falls back to the class-level annotation, never both

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: hasRole('ADMIN') re-adds the ROLE_ prefix and matches the role tag only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: hasAuthority('audio:delete'), hasAuthority('user:update'), hasAuthority('maqam:vote'), … — compares the one literal string it is given and adds no prefix

div.style: color: rgb(74, 58, 18) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Is that authority in the list

div.style: color: rgb(30, 58, 41) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Handler runs

div.style: color: rgb(92, 32, 24) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Package-scoped @RestControllerAdvice handleAccessDenied — ApiExceptionHandler for platform, GlobalExceptionHandler for user: extractRequiredAuthority regexes hasAuthority or hasRole out of the handler's @PreAuthorize into details.requiredAuthority, next to actor, actorAuthorities and requestMethod

div.style: color: rgb(92, 32, 24) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: JwtAccessDeniedHandler, the accessDeniedHandler wired in SecurityConfig: same body minus requiredAuthority. It only covers denials raised inside the filter chain, and every authorizeHttpRequests rule here is permitAll or authenticated — an unauthenticated caller gets 401 from JwtAuthenticationEntryPoint instead

div.style: color: rgb(92, 32, 24) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: 403 ACCESS_DENIED, category AUTHORIZATION
